newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FORECAST-News Corp Q1 seen rising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FORECAST-News Corp Q1 seen rising.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd is expected to report double digit growth in net profit before abnormals for its first financial quarter ended September 30 when it reports on Tuesday, Australian media analysts said.

Last month, Murdoch told the company's annual meeting the first quarter performance of his global media and entertainment group had been below expectations, but said he was still confident of a 20 percent profit rise in 1996/97.
Lachlan Drummond at First Pacific Stockbrokers forecast News Corp to report a net profit before abnormals of A$330 million for the first quarter and A$1.6 billion for the year to June 30.
"Mr Murdoch has already said it's not going to be 20 percent, so it is a bit of a guessing game what it is going to be. I think it will be around 17 percent," Drummond told Reuters.
News Corp's net operating profit before abnormal items fell 5.6 percent to A$284 million in the three months ended September 30, 1995, down from A$301 million a year earlier.

A Melbourne-based media analyst forecast News would report a pre-abnormal net profit of A$332 million, but the analyst said she would not be surprised if the group posts a first quarter below A$320 million.
"A lot of the gains will be due to films," the Melbourne analyst said referring to News' Independence Day blockbuster.
She said the market is quite confident that News would be able to increase its annual net profit above 20 percent.

"I think the majority of the market would be looking beyond that (20 percent)," she said. One Sydney-based media analyst forecast News Corp to report a net profit before abnormals of A$321 million, up 13 percent from the year-earlier quarter.
The film, television, publishing and newspaper conglomerate reported a six percent fall in pre-abnormals net profit to A$1.26 billion for the year to June 30, 1996.
One Sydney-based analyst said the last quarter is usually the strongest quarter for News Corp. He forecast a net profit before abnormals of A$1.545 billion for the 1996/97 year.
Murdoch said last month revenues at the Fox U.S. television business had begun 1996/97 slowly because of the Atlanta Olympic Games, the rights to which were held by the rival NBC network.
News would also get a boost in the first quarter from its 40 percent owned British Sky Broadcasting Plc.
The British pay TV operator reported a 31 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 66 million pounds and also reported a healthy rise in subscriber numbers.
One Melbourne-based analyst, who had not finalised his forecasts, said a strong first quarter was expected.

"I would have said something in the order of 15 percent in Australian dollar terms is quite reasonable, also remember the Australian dollar is a lot stronger so change to Aussie dollar (from other currencies) isn't as attractive," the analyst said.
News Corp shares closed three cents higher at A$7.17 on Friday. The shares have been rising steadily since hitting a 17 month low of A$6.03 on July 25.
